name: Gloria Mundi
history: A giant cooking apple first recorded in the USA in 1804, thought to have been raised in New York though a German origin has also been suggested. Its many names overlap with other huge apples: the National Fruit Collection lists Mère de Ménage as a synonym and vice versa, but the two are held as separate accessions and Bunyard considered them distinct. 'Pound' is also used for other big apples, including Fallawater.

look.description: Very large, broad, ribbed green-yellow apple, sometimes with a faint bronze blush.

taste.summary: Rather soft, coarse, yellowish to greenish flesh with a mild subacid flavour, somewhat dry; valued for size and cooking rather than taste.

tree.notes: Vigorous, spreading tree that USDA Geneva rates as unproductive; the heavy fruit needs a sheltered site.

climate.best_climates: Sheltered temperate gardens in eastern North America and southern England.
climate.poor_climates: Windy sites, where the huge fruit is blown down (inferred).

health.other: No disease ratings found; poor cropping is the main recorded fault.

grow_notes: Grown as a curiosity for its enormous fruit. Plant on a sheltered site and thin to single fruits per cluster so they reach full size.

name: Golden Nugget

origin.parentage: Golden Russet x Cox's Orange Pippin

history: Raised in 1932 by C.J. Bishop at Kentville, Nova Scotia, from Golden Russet crossed with Cox, and introduced in 1964. It was bred as a richly flavoured yellow dessert apple for maritime Canada.

look.description: Small, broadly conical golden apple with a long stalk, orange streaks and splashes, and plenty of russet.

taste.summary: Crisp, juicy flesh with a very sweet, rich and mellow flavour. Good fresh and excellent for pies, sauce and apple butter, but it does not keep long.

tree.notes: Spreading to drooping habit at Brogdale.

pollination.notes: Group 3 per Orange Pippin; Brogdale records early-May flowering.

climate.best_climates: Cool maritime climates such as Nova Scotia and the UK.
climate.poor_climates: Not documented; probably loses its rich flavour quickly in hot climates (inferred from short keeping).

health.other: No disease ratings found. Short storage life.

grow_notes: A good garden dessert apple for cool, damp climates. Eat or cook the crop within a few weeks of picking.

name: Guldborg
history: A Danish summer apple from the Guldborg district of Lolland, known by the 1870s and recorded by the Danish Pometet as a Maglemer seedling. It remains one of the best-known Lolland-Falster apples and is regarded in Denmark as a classic early cooking apple.

look.description: Tall, conical, strongly ribbed apple with a thin, greasy creamy-yellow skin, lightly flushed and flecked scarlet.

taste.summary: Firm white flesh with a subacid flavour that Brogdale's panel found evenly balanced between sweet and sharp but not very juicy; the Wikipedia list calls it aromatic. Mainly a cooking apple for late summer.

climate.best_climates: Cool Baltic and North Sea climates of Denmark and southern Scandinavia.
climate.poor_climates: Late-frost sites could damage its early blossom (inferred).

grow_notes: A regional heritage apple for cool northern gardens. Use the crop quickly in late summer for cooking.

name: Halberstädter Jungfernapfel
history: An old apple of the Harz area of central Germany, recorded in 1885. It is the mother of Geheimrat Breuhahn.

look.description: Tall, ribbed green to yellow apple blushed and striped orange-scarlet.

taste.summary: Firm, rather coarse pale cream flesh with a moderately sweet, subacid flavour. Brogdale's tasting panel rated it balanced but low in aroma and only moderately juicy.

grow_notes: A regional heritage apple for collectors; little practical growing information is published in English.

name: Hammerstein

origin.place: Royal Pomological Institute (Höhere Lehranstalt), Geisenheim, Germany

history: Raised from seed of Landsberger Reinette at Geisenheim in 1882 under Rudolph Goethe; it first fruited in 1891 and was sold from 1895. It was named after the Prussian agriculture minister Ernst von Hammerstein-Loxten and became a garden apple in Germany and northern Bohemia; it is the mother of Geheimrat Doktor Oldenburg.

look.description: Flattish, bluntly ribbed apple with a smooth, greasy yellowish-green skin ripening golden, finely speckled, with a faint washed brownish-orange cheek.

taste.summary: Very juicy, firm yellowish flesh with a sweet-subacid to tart, aromatic flavour that holds its quality through storage. Brogdale's panel found sweetness and acidity both fairly high and well balanced.
taste.best_eaten: Nov-Feb; does not shrivel in store

tree.notes: Strong when young, later moderate, making a broad round crown with plenty of short fruiting spurs; suits espaliers and small trained forms. Crops early and heavily but alternates; thin heavy sets to keep size up.

pollination.notes: Mid-season flowering at Brogdale (early May). Blossom is reported to be frost-resistant.

climate.best_climates: Cool central European climates; resistant to wood and blossom frost, so suited to colder German and Bohemian sites.
climate.poor_climates: Damp, disease-prone sites because of its scab, canker and woolly aphid susceptibility.

health.other: Susceptible to scab, canker and woolly aphid, moderately to mildew; fruit bruises easily and can rot in store. Overcropping gives small fruit.

grow_notes: Train as an espalier or small tree and thin fruitlets in heavy years. Needs a spray programme or an airy site against scab; handle fruit gently.

name: Herma

origin.place: Kaiser Wilhelm Institute, Müncheberg, Brandenburg, Germany
origin.raised_by: Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Breeding Research, Müncheberg

history: Raised in the 1930s at the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute in Müncheberg from a Jonathan seedling. Material later went to Poland's Skierniewice institute, the USDA in 1969 and the UK National Fruit Trials in 1977.

look.description: Large, ribbed, rounded yellow apple flushed and striped red over much of the skin, which can be tough.

taste.summary: Crisp, juicy cream flesh, slightly acid, with a delicate perfume; USDA records liken it to Northern Spy but rate the eating quality only fair.

tree.notes: Comes into bearing early with moderate productivity; drooping habit at Brogdale.

climate.best_climates: Central European continental climates with a long enough autumn to ripen a late-October apple.
climate.poor_climates: Short-season sites where a late-October apple cannot ripen (inferred).

grow_notes: A late keeper for collectors: leave on the tree until late October and store cool until winter.
